ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The distance of two not-crossing edges of a regular tetrahedron (triangular pyramid with all the six edges equal) is $6 \mathrm{~cm}$. What is the volume of the tetrahedron $\left(\right.$ in $\left.\mathrm{cm}^{3}\right)$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a regular tetrahedron. Two disjoint, non-intersecting opposite edges are marked with small dots, and a dashed segment connects these marked points, representing the shortest distance between the two opposite edges. Reasoning: Let the side length of the regular tetrahedron be a. In a regular tetrahedron, the shortest distance between two opposite edges is the segment joining their midpoints, and its length is a/√2. The given distance is 6 cm, so a/√2 = 6, hence a = 6√2. The volume of a regular tetrahedron is V = a^3/(6√2). Substituting a = 6√2 gives V = (6√2)^3/(6√2) = 72. Therefore the volume is 72 cm^3.

method.method_draft: Model the tetrahedron with coordinates as alternate vertices of a cube. From the diagram/text, treat the marked non-crossing edges as an opposite pair of edges of a regular tetrahedron. Place the tetrahedron at A=(k,k,k), B=(k,-k,-k), C=(-k,k,-k), D=(-k,-k,k). This is a regular tetrahedron. Compute the distance between opposite edges AB and CD using the skew-line distance formula; for these coordinates it equals 2k. Since the text gives this distance as 6, get k=3. Then compute the tetrahedron volume by the determinant formula V = |det(B-A, C-A, D-A)|/6. The determinant magnitude is 16k^3, so V = 16k^3/6 = 8k^3/3. With k=3, V = 72.

Following the assigned coordinate model, place the regular tetrahedron at alternate vertices of a cube: A=(k,k,k), B=(k,-k,-k), C=(-k,k,-k), D=(-k,-k,k). These four points form a regular tetrahedron. Consider the opposite edges AB and CD. Their direction vectors are B-A=(0,-2k,-2k) and D-C=(0,-2k,2k). The skew-line distance between AB and CD is |(C-A)·((B-A)×(D-C))| / |(B-A)×(D-C)|.
